texts: The classic Takeuchi operation uses a portion of the anterior wall of the pulmonary artery to build a baffle: E.
An aortopulmonary window is created and a tunnel made from a pulmonary artery flap carries aortic blood inside the pulmonary artery to the anomalous coronary ostium.
Today direct reimplantation of the left coronary into the aorta is preferred when possible; repair is done promptly, without waiting for recovery, since perfusion itself is the treatment.

Even infants with severe LV dysfunction and mitral regurgitation usually recover after revascularization, so transplantation and early mitral repair are rarely needed, and LIMA grafting is not the standard in children.
In the picture, Takeuchi's tunnel, cut from the money pipe's own front wall, leads the orca's water to the left spike.
Memory hook: Take-uchi takes a flap and builds a tunnel inside.
